exceptions.reason: The part writes no `data-disabled`. CSS selects the disabled state on the same element: `:disabled` on a native disabled button, and `[aria-disabled='true']` on a disabled button that keeps the focus and on each other element (rule 8.15). The family has no namespace of constants (rule 8.10).

`Button.test.ts` tests the element, the `element` slot, the form, the disabled states, the keys of an element that is not a native button and the fieldset. The part reads its element, so the cases of `nativeButton` render the element in the `element` slot. A native disabled button gets `pointerdown` and `pointerup`, and no `mousedown`, `mouseup` or `click` (`test/measurements/button.test.ts`). A disabled button that keeps the focus, and each other element, stops the same events, so the `pointerdown` listener of the developer runs. Its `keydown` listener runs too: a key activates a button only through `click`, and a part that holds the button needs Escape.
The prop only says what the developer renders (rule 8.3). The part reads the element that it renders, and `as` and the `element` slot render another element.
The part writes no `data-disabled`: `:disabled` and `[aria-disabled='true']` select the disabled state on the same element (rule 8.15). The family has no namespace of constants (rule 8.10).

surfaceAdditions.reason: The part reads `disabled` for its state and for the attributes of its element, so it is a declared prop. Base UI reads it from the native attributes of the button, and `types.md` has no row for a native attribute.
